text:
Eli S: Heads-up — working a POC with a large financial customer. Completely air-gapped DC. They want clarity on: packaging format (USB vs bundle), offline upgrade cadence, how licensing/activation works without internet, and whether we can fully disable telemetry for the POC. Also a pricing ask: can we offer monthly POC licensing instead of annual?

Priya R: We support two common workflows: a single signed offline bundle (tar.gz) that contains images + SBOM + delta layers, or a USB/shipyard delivery for very restricted sites. Bundles are chunked for large networks. SBOM and signatures are included (sigchain).

Priya R: For upgrades: we provide full bundle + delta patches. Cadence is customer-driven — POCs usually take a weekly/biweekly cadence for patches, production typically quarterly. For sealed sites we recommend explicit manual apply (no auto-updates).

Tom L: Technical: our offline update flow is: bootstrap image -> install operator -> apply bundle. Emergency hotfixes are supported as signed delta patches. We cannot initiate outbound connections from the customer side. Verify signature with: 

```
# verify bundle signature locally
rwdctl verify --bundle ./redwood-offline-2026-03.tar.gz --cert /opt/redwood/certs/authority.pem
```

Sara K: From security: telemetry can be disabled per-install. We have an opt-out flag for data-plane telemetry; audit logs remain local. KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys and allow offline key import. For sealed networks we need the customer's CA chain for cert rotation and a documented cert-rotation plan (rotation requires a planned maintenance window).

Eli S: Customer wants a written statement that no telemetry will leave their network during the POC and that we can provide SBOM + signed checksums. Can we provide that? Also, they asked if an ad-hoc hotfix within 48 hours is possible during the POC.

Priya R: We can provide an attestation (signed PDF) stating telemetry disabled and SBOM provided. For 48h hotfixes — for POCs we can commit to expedited signed patches (subject to legal SOW). Production emergency SLA needs enterprise add-on.

Tom L: Operational note: for 48h hotfix we still need a validated install footprint and remote access to accept patch files via their transfer method (USB or SFTP they host). We will stage a signed patch and deliver checksums. No push install from our side.

deploy-bot: build 2026.3.14.17 artifact rwd-bundle-2026-03-14-17 sha256: d3b07384d113edec49eaa6238ad5ff00 (signed).

Customer POC: Appreciate the detail. Two follow-ups: 1) licensing token flow — can you issue a time-limited offline license file? 2) If we need a hotfix during US business hours, can we pre-authorize a specific person to apply patches?

Priya R: 1) Yes — we can issue a time-limited license file (signed license blob) that is loaded locally. 2) Yes — we support a pre-authorized operator list and will include the key-fingerprint in the SOW.

Sara K: Reminder: we'll need to complete the security questionnaire with their SecOps and attach the MOU that covers telemetry, incident reporting (air-gapped procedures), and escalation contacts. Also ask legal for the POC pricing addendum if they want monthly billing.

Eli S: I'll schedule a sync with the customer for Monday and attach the attestation + sample license flow. @Tom L @Sara K @Priya R can we confirm: 48h expedited signed hotfix for POC (fee waived) — yes for this deal?

Tom L: Confirmed for the POC — engineering will prioritize. We require their install checksum and transfer mechanism before patch creation.

Sara K: Confirmed from security side, provided they sign the MOU and complete the questionnaire.

Priya R: I'll draft the SOW addendum for monthly POC billing and attach the sample attestations + SBOM verification steps.

Eli S: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll post the Monday meeting invite and include the checklist: SBOM, CA chain, transfer method (USB/SFTP), pre-authorized operators, and SOW signature. :thumbsup:
